study_goal: Measure observed Dutch VOC historical port-to-port connections from original voyages, and connect island port-level HOSTS/GBIF exploratory observations without claiming that particular plants were ship cargo
source: Leenstra & Parthesius (2022), Dutch Ships in Asian Waters in the 17th Century, IISG Data Collection V1
published_dataset_license: CC BY-SA custom dataset terms, verify full attribution and licensing before any redistribution
years: 1595–1687 published Dutch East India Company Asian voyage table; only dates verified from archive contents later
source_not_to_confuse: original VOC historic journeys vs 2020 AIS paths
main 51-island sample is mostly outside old Dutch East India Company routes
Dutch East Indies were not all colonized at voyage date
recorded voyage stopover is not documented plant propagule or larval host transportation
primary_next_gate: public 57,669-row file accessible and row schema identifies dated route origin/destination place identifiers; then map unique historical place names to named WPI port matches with manual/geospatial validation before comparing island taxa
cargo_and_plant_stratification: IISG dataset has separate cargo totaal.tab ~7737 observations and 5 variables; cannot claim historical transported plant names before inspecting actual cargo classifications
bias_protection: Do not interpret modern AIS-absent edges as no connection; do not use only successful mapped host-positive island links to select historical voyages; do not imply GBIF observations in 2001–2024 prove 17th-century plant introductions
